Evidence: Turner labels agāra- 'house' probably borrowed from Dravidian; DEDR 7 contains Ta. and Ma. akam 'inside, house, abode'.
Turner/EWA identifies iñcāka- 'prawn, shrimp' as Dravidian; DEDR 517 is the Dravidian prawn/shrimp set (Ta. iṟā/iṟāl, Te. reyya/royya), although the formal correspondence is not transparent.
Turner derives the ball/roll senses from Dravidian and explicitly compares Ta. uṇṭai, Ma. uṇḍa, and Ka./Tu. uṇḍe, all contained in DEDR 664.
Turner supports Dravidian origin for kalāpa- 'bundle, collection' with Ka. kalappu 'miscellaneous collection'; DEDR 1299 contains Ka. kalapu 'miscellaneous mass' in the *kal- 'mix, join' set.
Turner directs *kicca-/*kacca-/*khacca- 'mud, dirt' to unnamed Dravidian comparanda; DEDR 2020 *kec-aṯ- 'mud, slush' supplies the closest form-and-meaning match.

Turner/EWA derives kuṭhāra- 'axe' probably from Dravidian and connects it with √kuṭṭ; DEDR 2064 contains koṭṭ-/kuṭ- 'peck, strike, dig' and nouns for hoe or spade. Secondary main-entry comparison beside the existing appendix da32 link.

Turner/EWA derives kuḍava- 'grain measure' from Dravidian and states that its original sense was 'pot'; DEDR 1651 contains Ta. kuṭam, Ka. koḍa, and Te. kuḍaka 'pot, cup, bowl'. Secondary comparison beside the existing DEDR 1827 measure link.
Turner explicitly compares the pond/tank member kūla- with Ta. kuḷam 'tank'; this form belongs to DEDR 1828 *kuḷ-am 'tank, reservoir, lake'.
Turner derives kūpa- 'mooring post, mast' from Dravidian Ta./Ma. kūmpu and Tu. kūvè 'mast', the forms collected in DEDR 1895.
Editorial comparison of CDIAL *kōcc- 'thrust, pierce, dig' with DEDR 1859 Ka./Tu. koccu 'cut up or into pieces' and the wider *kuṟ-/koṟ- set 'cut, bore, excavate, pierce'.
DEDR 2207 explicitly compares Skt. koṭṭa-/koṭa- 'fort, stronghold'; the Dravidian entry contains Ta. kōṭṭai, Ma. kōṭṭa, Ka. kōṭe, Te. kōṭa and reconstructs *kōṭṭ-ay 'fort'.

Turner/EWA calls ghōṭa- 'horse' non-Aryan and probably Dravidian; DEDR 1711 is the kutirai/kudire/guṟṟamu horse set, but its note also allows Te. guṟṟamu to be borrowed from IA ghoṭaka-, so direction remains open.
DEDR 2448 explicitly compares Skt. candana- 'sandal'; the entry combines Ta. cāttu 'smear, anoint', cāntam/cāntu 'sandal (paste/wood)', and corresponding South Dravidian forms.
CDIAL treats daṇḍa- 'stick, staff; stalk, stem' as probably non-Aryan; DEDR 3056 contains Ta./Ma. taṇṭu, Ka. daṇṭu/daṇḍa, and Te. daṇṭu 'stalk, stem'.

Turner cites a Dravidian proposal for píṇḍa- 'lump; ball of rice'; DEDR 4162 contains Ta. piṇṭi and Te./Central Dravidian piṇḍi 'flour, meal, powder'. Direction is left open because the Dravidian nominal forms may reflect IA influence.

Editorial cross-reference for the classical proposal connecting pūjā- 'worship' with ritual smearing/anointing: DEDR 4352 Ta./Ma. pūcu, Ka. pūsu, Tu. pūjuni, Te. pūyu 'smear, anoint'. The proposal is contested, so no direction is asserted.
Turner derives agasti- 'Sesbania grandiflora' from Dravidian; DEDR 5 contains Ta. akatti, Tu. agase-mara/agasti, and other names for the same plant.
Turner derives *aḍḍi/*aḍi- 'heel' from Dravidian and explicitly cites Ta./Ka. aḍi and Te. aḍugu 'foot, footstep', the forms collected in DEDR 72.
Turner compares uḍupa- 'raft' with a probably Dravidian boat word and cites Ta. ōṭam; DEDR 1039 contains Ta./Ma. ōṭam 'boat, raft'.
Turner compares *ōḍḍh- 'put on, wear, cover' with Ta. uṭu-, Ka. uḍu-, and Te. uḍupu; DEDR 587 is the corresponding Dravidian 'put on clothes, dress' set.

Turner considers kaṇḍū- 'itching; sexual desire' Dravidian or Austroasiatic and cross-refers to kacchū-. DEDR 1104 contains Ka. kajji/gajji, Te. kasi, and related forms meaning 'itch' or 'itching, desire'; the formal connection and direction remain uncertain.
Turner treats kanda- 'bulbous root' as probably Dravidian; DEDR 1171 contains Ta. kaṇṭa and Ka. gaḍḍe/geḍḍe 'bulbous root', especially the root of the lotus.
Turner derives karōṭi- 'cup, skull' probably from Dravidian and explicitly cites Ta. ciraṭṭai 'coconut shell, begging bowl', the form recorded in DEDR 2550.
Turner considers kavāṭa-/kapāṭa- 'door leaf' probably Dravidian; DEDR 1187 contains Ta. katavu/katavam, Ma. katavu/kataku, and Ka. kadavu 'door, door leaf'.
Turner derives kāṇḍa- 'joint of a plant' probably from Dravidian and cites Ta. kaṇ; DEDR 1160 contains Ta./Ka. kaṇ and Te. kaṇupu 'joint or node of bamboo or cane'.
Turner derives kuṇḍa- 'bowl, waterpot, basin' from Dravidian and cites Ta. kuṭam and Ka. guṇḍi; DEDR 1651 contains the Dravidian pot, pitcher, and vessel family.
For the 'nest' sense of kulāya-, Turner cites Ta. kūṭu and Ka./Te./Tu. gūḍu; these forms constitute DEDR 1883 'nest, cage, hollow'.
For the 'woven receptacle, basket' sense of kulāya-, Turner cites Ta. kuṭai, Ma. kūṭa, Ka./Tu. gūḍe, and Te. gūḍa; DEDR 1884 is the corresponding basket set.
Turner derives kulya- 'winnowing basket' from Dravidian through the kulāya- comparison; DEDR 1884 contains the cited Dravidian basket family.
Turner derives kūrdati 'leaps, jumps' probably from Dravidian and explicitly cites Ta. kuti and Ka. gudi 'jump, spring', the forms collected in DEDR 1705.
Turner derives gulpha-/kulpha- 'ankle' from Dravidian and cites Ta. kuḷampu 'hoof'; DEDR 1829 also includes Toda kwïḷx 'lower leg joints down to the hoof, wrist'.
Turner considers gōdhā- 'large lizard, iguana' probably Dravidian but remodeled by folk etymology; DEDR 592 contains Ta./Ma. uṭumpu 'iguana'.

Turner discusses Dravidian and Munda analyses of tundi-/tuṇḍi- 'navel'; DEDR 624 contains Ta. unti and Ma. unti/tunti 'navel, belly'. Direction is left open because the source attribution is explicitly disputed.

Turner includes paṅgu- 'lame, crippled' among possibly Dravidian or Munda words for bodily defects; DEDR 1688 is the widespread Dravidian kuṇṭ-/kuṇṭi 'be lame, limp; cripple' family, but the formal match is weak.
